PREAMBLE: Policy and Guidelines

Purpose

The San Andreas Penal Code serves as the primary legal framework governing criminal acts, enforcement procedures, and penalties within the jurisdiction of the State of San Andreas. This document outlines policies and guidelines designed to ensure justice, maintain public order, and uphold constitutional rights.

______________________________________________________________________________

DEFINITIONS

CHAPTER 1 GENERAL PURPOSE

The main objectives of this chapter are to:

  1. Establish the foundational principles of the San Andreas Penal Code.
  2. Define the purpose and scope of criminal law enforcement within the state.
  3. Provide clear guidance for law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and judicial authorities in the application of state laws.
  4. Ensure consistency and fairness in criminal proceedings and the administration of justice.
  5. Protect the rights and safety of all residents, visitors, and entities within San Andreas.
  6. Promote public order and deterrence, reducing crime through a transparent and predictable legal framework.
  7. Support the legislative intent of maintaining a lawful, safe, and just society.

CHAPTER 2 GENERAL DEFINITIONS

Section 2.1 – Person

  • “Person” includes any individual, citizen, visitor, or resident within the jurisdiction of San Andreas.
  • This term also includes legal entities such as corporations, partnerships, and associations, unless the context specifies otherwise.

Section 2.2 – Law Enforcement Officer

  • A “Law Enforcement Officer” is any individual officially empowered to enforce the laws of San Andreas.
  • This includes:
  1. Police Officers and Deputies of local or county jurisdictions.
  2. State Troopers or Highway Patrol Officers.
  3. Other sworn officers are legally authorized to perform arrests and maintain public order.

Section 2.3 – Government employee

  • A"Government employee" refers to any on-duty employee of a local, state, or federal agency

Section 2.4 – Offense

  • An “Offense” is any act or omission prohibited by the San Andreas Penal Code or other applicable laws, and is punishable by fine, imprisonment, or other penalties.

Section 2.5 – Felony

  • A Felony is a serious criminal offense punishable by more than one year of imprisonment, substantial fines, or both.

Section 2.6 – Misdemeanor

  • A Misdemeanor is a less severe criminal offense not punishable by imprisonment or punishable by up to one year of imprisonment, a fine, or both.

Section 2.7 – Infraction

  • An Infraction is a minor violation of the law, not punishable by imprisonment.
  • Infractions typically result in fines, warnings, or administrative penalties.

Section 2.8 – Attempt

  • An “Attempt” occurs when a person intends to commit an offense and takes a direct step toward it, even if the crime is not completed.

Section 2.9 – Accomplice

  • An “Accomplice” is any person who knowingly assists, facilitates, or encourages another individual to commit an offense.

Section 3.0 – Weapon

  • A “Weapon” is defined as any object, device, instrument, or substance that is designed, manufactured, or modified with the primary purpose of inflicting death or serious bodily harm, or used or intended to be used in a manner capable of causing death, serious bodily injury, or destruction of property, whether lethal or non-lethal. There are three types of weapons classes:
  • Class 1 : Weapons commonly owned by civilians, with moderate risk, and generally legal with or without a standard license. Ex; Pistol .50, ceramic pistol, X17, machine Pistol, ST84 Skulln Sword, MX18 Classyblue
  • Class 2 : Weapons with greater lethality or rapid-fire capability Ex; Mini SMG, Micro SMG, SMG, Navy Revolver, KVR, Pump Shotgun, Revolver black Sawn Of Shotgun, SDR,7 VTN33 Graveshift,
  • Class 3 : Weapons intended for military use, highly lethal, or capable of mass destruction for Ex ; Double Action, Assault Rifle, Carbine Rifle, MB47, AGC, BK12, Dragon Scarl, Godzilla, AK47, Purplefunk AKT ,Foolv2 RED, M6A9 Diamond Soul,Scarl Rusty, M4 T Neon Integrale
  • Government-issue Firearm : Any firearm officially owned, issued, or provided by a government agency to a sworn law enforcement officer, military personnel, or authorized government employee

Section 3.1 – Firearm

  • A “firearm”, also referred to as a “gun”, is any weapon designed to expel a projectile through explosive force or combustion, and is capable of causing death or serious injury.

Section 3.2 – Machine Gun

  • A machine gun is a type of firearm capable of fully automatic fire, meaning it can continuously discharge multiple rounds with a single pull of the trigger until the trigger is released, the ammunition is depleted, or the weapon malfunctions. Unlike semi-automatic firearms, which fire one round per trigger pull, a machine gun is specifically designed for rapid and sustained fire, making it significantly more lethal and dangerous in both offensive and defensive use. Under most state and federal laws, machine guns are considered highly restricted or prohibited for civilian ownership due to their capacity for mass harm, and possession, sale, or transfer without proper authorization or licensing is typically classified as a serious felony offense.

Section 3.3 – Destructive Devices

  • A destructive device is any explosive, incendiary, or chemical weapon designed or intended to cause significant property damage, injury, or death, including but not limited to bombs, grenades, rockets, missiles, mines, Molotov cocktails, and other similar devices capable of mass destruction or widespread harm. This definition also encompasses any firearm or launcher with a bore greater than one-half inch in diameter that is not generally recognized as suitable for sporting purposes, as well as any combination of parts intended to assemble such a device. Destructive devices are considered highly restricted or prohibited under both state and federal law, and the unauthorized possession, manufacture, sale, transport, or use of such devices constitutes a serious felony offense due to the extreme threat they pose to public safety and security.

Section 3.4 – MDT

  • MDT stands for Mobile Data Terminal A portable or vehicle-mounted computer system that allows police officers, emergency responders, or government agents to access and input data directly into their agency’s database in real time.

Section 3.5 – HUT

  • Hold Until Trial (HUT) is a pre-trial detention status in which a suspect remains in custody until their court hearing or trial due to the severity of the offense or the risk they pose to public safety. A suspect may be held under HUT status if they are considered a flight risk, likely to commit further crimes, or pose a danger to the community or witnesses.

Section 3.6 – Serious Body Harm

  • Serious Bodily Harm is any physical injury that creates a substantial risk of death, causes long-term or permanent disfigurement, results in the loss or significant impairment of a body part or organ, or otherwise requires extensive medical treatment or hospitalization. Injuries that constitute serious bodily harm may include major fractures, deep lacerations, severe burns, or internal organ damage, and this level of harm is generally associated with aggravated offenses and can elevate a crime to a felony or higher penalty class.

Section 3.7 – Controlled Substance

  • A Controlled Substance is any drug, chemical, or substance whose manufacture, possession, distribution, or use is regulated by law, and which is classified into specific schedules or categories based on its medical value, potential for abuse, and risk to public health. There are three types of Controlled Substance in San Andreas State:
  • Schedule I : Weed bag / Cannabis / Marijuana/ Opium
  • Schedule II : Methamphetamine,  Cocaine
  • Schedule III : It is unknown what needs to be checked in the laboratory.

CHAPTER 3 CRIMINAL TERM DEFINITIONS

  • “Contraband” – Any item that is illegal to possess, transport, or distribute under the law.
  • “Deadly Force” – Means the force that is capable of causing death or serious bodily injury, including the use of firearms or other deadly weapons.
  • “Detention” – Means the act of lawfully holding a person in custody or restricting their freedom of movement for investigative or protective purposes.
  • “Arrest” – Using legal authority to take a person into custody. An arrest is generally made when there is probable cause that the individual has committed a crime.
  • “Force” – Power, violence, or pressure exerted against a person or thing to compel compliance or overcome resistance.
  • “Malice Aforethought” – The conscious and intentional decision to commit an act that the offender knows is unlawful and likely to cause harm.
  • “Risk” – The potential danger, hazard, or likelihood of harm or damage resulting from an action or situation.
  • “Probable Cause” – Reasonable grounds based on facts and circumstances that would lead a prudent person to believe a crime has been or is being committed.
  • “Accessory” – A person who aids, assists, or facilitates another in committing a crime, either before or after the fact.

CHAPTER 4 GOVERNMENT MEMBER CATEGORY

[Category 1 and Category 2 Government Officials possess a special legal status and, when acting within the scope of their official duties, are not subject to ordinary legal treatment, are entitled to enhanced protection and official immunity, and any act of violence, coercion, detention, kidnapping, or hostage taking against them shall constitute an offense against governmental authority.]

CATEGORY 1  CONSTITUTIONAL OFFICERS

Officials whose offices, authority, and existence are expressly established by the Constitution State. These officers exercise core sovereign powers of government and operate at the highest level of authority within their respective branches.

  • President of San Andreas
  • Vice President of San Andreas
  • Attorney General
  • Deputy Attorney General
  • Chief of Justice
  • Deputy Chief of Justice
  • Secretary of State
  • San Andreas State Legislature
  • Inspector General

CATEGORY 2  EXECUTIVE APPOINTED OFFICIALS

Officials who are appointed by constitutional officers to carry out executive, administrative, regulatory, or law enforcement functions, and who are directly accountable to executive authority.

  • Chief of Police
  • County Sheriff
  • Police Commissioner
  • Justice Judge
  • Medical Commissioner
  • State Attorney
  • Correctional Head Warden

CATEGORY 3  GOVERNMENT OPERATIVE OFFICERS

Government officials who perform day to day operational, enforcement, prosecutorial, or support functions, acting under the supervision of higher executive authority, and without independent policy-making power.

  • Assistant State Attorney
  • Police Officer
  • Deputy Sheriff
  • State Trooper
  • Correctional Officer
  • Medical Officer
  • Government Staff

PRINCIPLES OF CRIMINAL LIABILITY

CHAPTER 4 CULPABILITY

Section 4.1 – Definition of Culpability

  • “Culpability” – The degree to which a person can be held legally responsible for their actions or omissions under the law.

Section 4.2 – Levels of Culpability

  • Intent – A conscious decision to perform an act with the purpose of achieving a specific unlawful result.
  • Knowledge – Awareness that one’s conduct is of a particular nature or that certain circumstances exist which make the act unlawful.
  • Recklessness – Acting with conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk that harm or illegal consequences will result.
  • Negligence – Failure to exercise the care that a reasonable person would in the same situation, resulting in harm or unlawful consequences.

Section 4.3 – Special Culpability Doctrines

  • “Strict Liability” – Legal responsibility for an act regardless of intent, knowledge, or negligence, typically applied to specific statutory offenses.
  • “Willful Blindness” – Deliberate avoidance of knowledge of a fact or circumstance to escape legal responsibility.
  • “Complicity” – Participation in the commission of a crime by aiding, abetting, or encouraging another person to commit the offense.

CHAPTER 5 GENERAL PRINCIPLES ASSOCIATED TO REQUIREMENTS & EXEMPTIONS

Section 5.1 – Legal Requirements

All individuals are required to comply with state and federal laws governing conduct, possession, and activity within the jurisdiction of San Andreas. Any act or omission that violates statutory requirements constitutes a criminal offense unless otherwise exempted by law.

Section 5.2 – Licensing and Authorization

Certain activities, including but not limited to the possession of firearms, operation of specific vehicles, or conduct of regulated businesses, require a valid license or government authorization. Engaging in such activities without proper licensing constitutes an offense unless the individual falls under a recognized legal exemption.

Section 5.3 – Lawful Exemptions

A lawful exemption is a circumstance recognized by statute or regulation that shields an individual from criminal liability for actions that would otherwise constitute an offense. These exemptions may include law enforcement duties, emergency actions, or other lawful activities carried out under government authority.

Section 5.4 – Burden of Proof for Exemptions

The individual claiming an exemption bears the responsibility of demonstrating that the exemption applies, unless a statute specifically provides otherwise. Law enforcement and the court may require documentary or testimonial evidence to validate the exemption.

Section 5.5 – Immunity Under Law

Certain individuals may be granted immunity from prosecution under specific conditions defined by law, including government officials acting within the scope of their duties, persons cooperating under immunity agreements, or individuals protected by statutory immunity provisions.

______________________________________________________________________________

DEFENSE

CHAPTER 6 DEFENSES IN GENERAL

Section 6.1 – Burden of Proof

The burden of establishing a defense may rest with either the defendant or the prosecution, depending on statutory requirements. Certain defenses, such as self-defense, require the defendant to present sufficient evidence to raise the defense, after which the prosecution must disprove it beyond a reasonable doubt.

CHAPTER 7 DEFENSE IN INFANCY

Section 7.1 – Infancy

  • Except as provided in subdivision two of this section, a person less than sixteen years old is not criminally responsible for conduct.
  • A person thirteen, fourteen, or fifteen years of age is criminally responsible for acts constituting murder in the second degree as defined in subdivisions one and two of Section 125.25, and in subdivision three of such section, provided that the underlying conduct meets the statutory elements.
  • In any prosecution for an offense, lack of criminal responsibility by reason of infancy, as defined in this section, constitutes a complete defense.

CHAPTER 8 DEFENSE OF JUSTIFICATION

Section 8.1 – General Rule of Justification

Conduct that would otherwise constitute an offense is justified and not criminally liable when it is performed under circumstances recognized by law as necessary to prevent a greater harm or to protect lawful interests, as set forth in this chapter.

Section 8.2 – Self‑Defense

A person may use physical force upon another when and to the extent they reasonably believe it is necessary to defend themselves from the imminent use of unlawful physical force by that other person.

  • The use of deadly physical force is only justified if the person reasonably believes that the aggressor is using or about to use deadly physical force, or is committing a forcible felony such as robbery, burglary, kidnapping, or rape.
  • There is no duty to retreat if the person is in their own dwelling and not the initial aggressor.

Section 8.3 – Defense of Others

A person may use physical force to defend another individual under the same circumstances in which they would be justified to defend themselves. The use of deadly physical force in defense of others is only justified when the defender reasonably believes the third person is in imminent danger of deadly physical force or a forcible felony.

Section 8.4 – Defense of Premises

A person may use reasonable physical force to prevent or terminate a trespass or unlawful entry upon their premises.

  • Deadly force may only be used to prevent arson, burglary, or when the intruder poses an imminent threat of deadly harm to the occupants.

Section 8.5 – Limitation of Justification

The defense of justification is not available to:

  • A person who is the initial aggressor, unless they withdraw and communicate that withdrawal.
  • A person who provokes the use of force with the intent to cause injury or death.
  • Situations where reckless or negligent injury to an innocent third party occurs during the use of force.

CHAPTER 9 OTHER DEFENSES INVOLVING LACK OF CULPABILITY

Section 9.1 – General Rule

A defendant may assert a defense based on lack of culpability if they can demonstrate that, due to their mental state, condition, or other legally recognized circumstance, they could not form the requisite intent or mental state required to commit the offense.

Section 9.2 – Insanity Defense

  • A person is not criminally responsible for conduct if, at the time of the act, as a result of severe mental disease or defect, they did not know the nature and quality of the act or did not know that it was wrong.
  • This defense must be supported by competent medical or psychiatric evidence, and the burden of proof may vary according to statute.
  • If established, the court may order commitment to a secure mental health facility rather than standard incarceration.

Section 9.3 – Involuntary Intoxication

  • Conduct is excused when the actor was involuntarily intoxicated and, as a result, lacked the capacity to know or appreciate the nature of the act or that the act was wrong.
  • Involuntary intoxication includes:
  • Intoxication caused by fraud, duress, or medical necessity, and
  • Intoxication without the actor’s knowledge or consent.

Section 9.4 – Duress

  • A person is not criminally liable for conduct if they acted under the compulsion of a present, imminent, and impending threat of death or serious bodily injury, which a reasonable person would be unable to resist.

  • Limitations:
  • Duress is not available if the defendant recklessly placed themselves in a situation where duress was probable.
  • Duress is not a defense to homicide in most jurisdictions.

Section 9.5 – Entrapment

  • Entrapment occurs when law enforcement or their agents induce or persuade a person to commit an offense they were not otherwise predisposed to commit.
  • Mere opportunity provided by law enforcement does not constitute entrapment; there must be improper inducement or pressure.

Section 9.6 – Mistake or Ignorance of Fact

  • A mistake of fact is a defense if the mistake negates the mental state required to establish the offense.
  • Mistake of law is generally not a defense, except where:
  • The law was not reasonably available, or
  • The defendant reasonably relied on an official interpretation later found to be invalid.

TITLE 0. OFFENSES AGAINST THE AUTHORITY OF THE STATE

(0)01. Treason

Treason is the gravest offense against the State, committed by any person who levies war against the State, adheres to its enemies, or provides them with aid and comfort. A conviction requires clear and direct intent to betray the nation and support hostile forces, either foreign or domestic.

(0)01. Treason is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(0)02. Sedition

Any person who willfully incites, organizes, or participates in actions intended to ++overthrow or undermine the lawful authority of the State of San Andreas through unlawful force, riot, or insurrection is guilty of sedition.

(0)02. Sedition is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(0)03. Rebellion and Insurrection

Any person who knowingly participates in, organizes, or assists with an armed uprising, violent disturbance, or organized resistance against the lawful government of the State of San Andreas commits the offense of rebellion and insurrection. This includes any coordinated attempt to seize government facilities, prevent government operations, or remove lawfully established authority through force or violence.

(0)03. Rebellion and Insurrection is categorized as a felony and is punishable byCourt Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(0)04. Sabotage of State Functions

Any person who intentionally damages, destroys, obstructs, or interferes with government property, infrastructure, or official operations of the State of San Andreas, with the intent to impair, hinder, or disrupt state authority or autonomy, commits the crime of sabotage. This includes but is not limited to the destruction of state communication networks, security systems, emergency response infrastructure, or critical facilities used for public safety or government operations.

(0)04. Sabotage of State Functions  is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(0)05. Unlawful Impersonation of State Authority

Any person who falsely represents themselves as a government official, law enforcement officer, judge, or any individual with lawful state authority, or performs acts reserved exclusively for such authority without legal authorization, commits the crime of unlawful impersonation. This includes issuing false documents, conducting unlawful arrests, or exercising powers exclusive to the state.

(0)05. Unlawful Impersonation of State Authority is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(0)06. Espionage

Any person who knowingly and willfully gathers, transmits, or delivers information relating to the security, defense, or governmental operations of the State of San Andreas to any foreign entity, hostile organization, or unauthorized individual, with the intent to harm the State or aid its adversaries, commits the offense of espionage. This includes infiltration of government facilities, unauthorized access to classified documents, or the use of electronic means to obtain restricted information for unlawful purposes.

(0)06. Espionage is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(0)07. Terrorism

Any person who commits or attempts to commit an act dangerous to human life, property, or critical infrastructure, in violation of criminal law, and who does so with the intent to intimidate or coerce a civilian population, influence the policy of a government, or affect the conduct of government by mass destruction, assassination, or kidnapping, where such act involves foreign direction, control, support, or transnational elements, commits the offense of Terrorism.

(0)07. Terrorism is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(0)08. Domestic Terrorism

Any person who commits or attempts to commit an act dangerous to human life, property, or critical infrastructure, in violation of criminal law, and who does so with the intent to intimidate or coerce a civilian population, influence the policy of a government, or affect the conduct of government by mass destruction, assassination, or kidnapping, where such act occurs primarily within the territorial jurisdiction of the State and without foreign direction or control, commits the offense of Domestic Terrorism.

(0)08. Domestic Terrorism is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(0)09. Complicity of State Enemies

Any person who, without being the primary organizer or mastermind, knowingly provides material support, specialized equipment, or active assistance to any individual committing an offense under TITLE 0. This includes, but is not limited to, providing technical expertise, surveillance, or physical labor to facilitate the execution of the crime, while acting under the direction or influence of another.

(0)09. Complicity of State Enemies is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 60 Months in prison with a fine of $350,000.

TITLE 1. OFFENSES AGAINST THE PERSON

(1)01. Criminal Threats

Any person who willfully threatens to commit a crime of violence with the intent to place another in reasonable fear for their safety commits criminal threats.

(1)01. Criminal Threats is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $6,000.

(1)02. Assault

Any person who unlawfully threatens or attempts to use physical force against another person, without actually touching them, commits assault.

(1)02. Assault is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 12 Months in prison with a fine of $6,500.

(1)03. Assault on a Government Employee

Any person who commits assault against a known, on-duty government employee (such as a police officer or judge) commits this offense.

(1)03. Assault on a Government Employee is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $35,000.

(1)04. Assault with Deadly Weapon

Any person who commits assault using a firearm, knife, or any other weapon capable of causing severe harm or death commits this offense.

(1)04. Assault with Deadly Weapon is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 22 Months in prison with a fine of $28,000

(1)05. Aggravated assault on a Government Employee

Any person who commits assault using a deadly weapon against a known, on-duty government employee commits this offense.

(1)05. Aggravated assault on a Government Employee is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 35 Months in prison with a fine of $43,500

(1)06. Domestic Violence

Any person who assaults or batters a spouse, intimate partner, cohabitant, or family member commits domestic violence. Emotional relationships or shared residence may establish domestic status.

(1)06. Domestic Violence is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 50 Months in prison with a fine of $32,000

(1)07. Battery

Any person who intentionally makes unlawful physical contact with another person, resulting in an offensive touch or minor injury, commits battery.

(1)07. Battery is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 16 Months in prison with a fine of $35,000

(1)08. Battery on a Government Employee

Any person who intentionally makes unlawful physical contact on a Government Employee, resulting in an offensive touch or minor injury, commits battery

(1)08. Battery on a Government Employee is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $65,000

(1)09. Aggravated Battery

Any person who commits battery that causes serious bodily harm, permanent injury, or involves the use of a deadly weapon commits aggravated battery.

The use of a deadly weapon is what distinguishes aggravated battery from simple battery.

(1)09. Aggravated Battery is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 35 Months in prison with a fine of $50,000

(1)10. Gang Related Shooting

Any person who knowingly discharges a firearm at another person, an occupied vehicle, or dwelling in connection with gang activity, regardless of injury, commits this offense.

(1)10. Gang Related Shooting is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $30,000

(1)11. Attempted Second Degree Murder

Any person who attempts to unlawfully kill another without premeditation, but with malice, commits attempted second degree murder.

(1)11. Attempted Second Degree Murder is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 45 Months in prison with a fine of $59,000

(1)12. Attempted First Degree Murder

Any person who attempts to unlawfully kill another with premeditation and malice aforethought commits attempted first degree murder.

(1)12. Attempted First Degree Murder is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 60 Months in prison with a fine of $85,000

(1)13. Attempted Murder of Government Employee

Any person who attempts to unlawfully kill a government employee performing lawful duties commits this offense.

(1)13. Attempted Murder of Government Employee is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 80 Months in prison with a fine of $160,000

(1)14. Third Degree Murder

Any person who unlawfully causes the death of another through reckless conduct or depraved indifference commits third degree murder.

(1)14. Third Degree Murder is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 150 Months in prison with a fine of $180.000

(1)15. Second Degree Murder

Any person who unlawfully kills another without premeditation, but with malice aforethought, commits second degree murder..

(1)15. Second Degree Murder is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 470 Months in prison with a fine of $200,000

(1)16. First Degree Murder

Any person who unlawfully kills another with malice aforethought and premeditation commits first degree murder.

(1)16. First Degree Murder is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(1)17. Murder of a Government Employee

Any person who unlawfully kills a government employee engaged in lawful duties commits this offense.

(1)17. Murder of a Government Employee is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(1)18. Serial Homicide

Any person who unlawfully kills two or more individuals in separate incidents over a period of time commits serial homicide.

(1)18. Serial Homicide is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(1)19. Mayhem

Any person who unlawfully and maliciously disfigures, disables, or permanently injures another’s body part commits mayhem.

(1)19. Mayhem is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 85 Months in prison with a fine of $60,000

(1)20. Aggravated Mayhem

Any person who commits mayhem with intent to cause permanent disability or disfigurement commits aggravated mayhem.

(1)20. Aggravated Mayhem is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(1)21. Torture

Any person who inflicts extreme physical pain and suffering upon another for purposes of punishment, coercion, or sadistic pleasure commits torture.

(1)21. Torture is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(1)22. Unlawful Imprisonment

Any person who unlawfully restrains or confines another without legal authority commits unlawful imprisonment.

(1)22. Unlawful Imprisonment is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $3,500

(1)23. Unlawful Detention

Any person who unlawfully detains another by force or threat, restricting their movement without legal authority, commits unlawful detention.

(1)23. Unlawful Detention is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $20,000

(1)24. Hostages

Any person to take, restrain, or hold one or two individuals as hostages with intent to compel any act or omission, evade lawful arrest, or affect governmental action or decision-making.

(1)24. Hostages is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $6,000

(1)25. Aggravated Hostages

Any person to take or detain three or more individuals as hostages for the purpose of coercion, evasion of lawful arrest, or interference with governmental action, and such conduct shall constitute aggravated hostage taking.

(1)25. Aggravated Hostages is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 35 Months in prison with a fine of $20,000

(1)26. Hostage Taking of Government Employees Category 1

Any person who unlawfully seizes, confines, restrains, or holds a Category 1 Government Officer as a hostage, with intent to compel any act or omission, to influence governmental authority, to affect constitutional functions, or to avoid lawful arrest or prosecution, commits the offense of Hostage Taking of a Constitutional Officer.

(1)26. Hostage Taking of Government Employees Category 1 is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(1)27. Hostage Taking of Government Employees Category 2

Any person who unlawfully seizes, confines, restrains, or holds a Category 2 Government Official as a hostage, for the purpose of coercing governmental action, obstructing executive operations, facilitating escape, or avoiding lawful arrest or prosecution, commits the offense of Hostage Taking of an Executive Government Official.

(1)27. Hostage Taking of Government Employees Category 2 is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 100 Months in prison with a fine of $120,000

(1)28. Hostage Taking of Government Employees Category 3

Any person who unlawfully seizes, confines, restrains, or holds a Category 3 Government Operative Officer as a hostage, while such officer is engaged in or targeted because of the performance of official duties, and does so to compel action, evade lawful arrest, facilitate escape, or obstruct governmental functions, commits the offense of Hostage Taking of a Government Operative Officer.

(1)28. Hostage Taking of Government Employees Category 3 is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 80 Months in prison with a fine of $100,000

(1)29. Aggravated Hostage Taking of Government Employees

Any person who unlawfully seizes, confines, restrains, more government employees or public officers as hostages, under aggravating circumstances, including but not limited to the taking of four or more hostages, the use or threat of deadly force, the infliction of serious bodily injury, prolonged or fortified detention, or substantial interference with governmental or law-enforcement functions, and who does so with intent to compel any act or omission, influence governmental action or decision-making, facilitate escape, or avoid lawful arrest or prosecution, commits the offense of Aggravated Hostage Taking of Government Employees.

(1)29. Aggravated Hostage Taking of Government Employees is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(1)30. Kidnapping

Any person who forcibly seizes, confines, or carries away another without consent and legal authority commits kidnapping.

(1)30. Kidnapping is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 14 Months in prison with a fine of $15,000

(1)31. Kidnapping of a Government Employee

Any person who kidnaps a government employee performing lawful duties commits this offense.

(1)31. Kidnapping of a Government Employee is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $45,000

(1)32. Aggravated Battery of a Government Employee

Any person who intentionally makes unlawful physical contact with a government employee, resulting in serious bodily harm, permanent injury, or involving the use of a deadly weapon, commits aggravated battery of a government employee. .

(1)32. Aggravated Battery of a Government Employee is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 45 Months in prison with a fine of $90,000

(1)33. Aggravated Hostage Taking Resulting in Medical Endangerment

Any person who knowingly seizes, detains, confines, restrains, or holds another person as a hostage, and intentionally or recklessly prevents, delays, or interferes with necessary medical treatment for such hostage while knowing, or having reason to know, that the hostage is suffering from serious bodily injury, a life-threatening condition, or requires immediate medical attention, commits the offense of Aggravated Hostage Taking Resulting in Medical Endangerment.

(1)33. Aggravated Hostage Taking Resulting in Medical Endangerment is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 90 Months in prison with a fine of $120,000

____________________________________________________________________________

TITLE 2. SEXUAL OFFENSES AND CRIMES AGAINST PUBLIC DECENCY

(2)01. Stalking

Any person who willfully and repeatedly follows, harasses, or threatens another person in a manner that would cause a reasonable individual to fear for their safety or the safety of their immediate family commits stalking.

(2)01. Stalking is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $2,000

(2)02. Harassment

Any person who engages in repeated or severe conduct that intimidates, threatens, or alarms another individual without lawful purpose commits harassment.

(2)02. Harassment is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(2)03. Sexual Assault

Any person who unlawfully touches, gropes, or otherwise engages in sexual contact with another without consent, by force, threat, or intimidation commits sexual assault.

(2)03. Sexual Assault is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $30,000

(2)04. Sexual Battery

Any person who willfully and unlawfully uses force or violence to commit sexual contact against another without consent commits sexual battery.

(2)04. Sexual Battery is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 50 Months in prison with a fine of $50,000

(2)05. Indecent Exposure

Any person who willfully exposes their genitals in public or in the presence of another person to offend or sexually gratify commits indecent exposure.

(2)05. Indecent Exposure is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $2,500

(2)06. Lewd or Dissolute Conduct

Any person who engages in lewd, lascivious, or sexually offensive acts in public, or in a manner likely to be observed by others, commits lewd or dissolute conduct.

(2)06. Lewd or Dissolute Conduct  is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $8,000

(2)07. Prostitution

Any person who agrees to, engages in, or offers sexual conduct for money or other consideration commits prostitution.

(2)07. Prostitution is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 65 Months in prison with a fine of $60,000

(2)08. Pandering/Pimping

Any person who recruits, encourages, or profits from the prostitution of another person, or controls their earnings, commits pandering or pimping.

(2)08. Pandering/Pimping is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(2)09. Rape

Any person who engages in sexual intercourse with another without consent, by force, threat, intimidation, or when the victim is incapacitated, commits rape.

(2)09. Rape is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(2)10. Rape Statutory

Any person who engages in sexual intercourse with a minor under the legal age of consent, regardless of consent, commits statutory rape.

(2)10. Rape Statutory is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(2)11. Human Trafficking

Any person who recruits, harbors, transports, provides, or obtains another person for labor or sexual exploitation through force, fraud, or coercion commits human trafficking.

(2)11. Human Trafficking is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(2)12. Forced Coercion

Any person who compels another to perform labor, services, or sexual acts against their will through threats, intimidation, or abuse of authority commits forced coercion.

(2)12. Forced Coercion is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(2)13. Minor Alcohol / Tobacco Violation

Any minor who unlawfully possesses or consumes alcohol or tobacco products commits a minor alcohol/tobacco violation.

(2)13. Minor Alcohol / Tobacco Violation is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(2)14. Minor Pornography Violation

Any person under 18 who unlawfully possesses, creates, or distributes explicit material depicting minors commits a minor pornography violation.

(2)14. Minor Pornography Violation is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $20,000

(2)15. Sale of Pornography to a Minor

Any person who knowingly sells, distributes, or provides pornographic materials to a minor commits this offense.

(2)15. Sale of Pornography to a Minor is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $15,000

(2)16. Sale of Alcohol/Tobacco to A Minor

Any person who knowingly sells or furnishes alcohol or tobacco products to a minor commits this offense.

(2)16. Sale of Alcohol/Tobacco to A Minor is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 12 Months in prison with a fine of $7,000

(2)17. Child Neglect

Any parent or guardian who willfully fails to provide necessary care, supervision, or protection for a minor, endangering the child’s health or safety, commits child neglect.

(2)17. Child Neglect is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(2)18. Child Abuse

Any person who willfully inflicts physical injury, cruel punishment, or sexual abuse upon a child commits child abuse.

(2)18. Child Abuse is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, Court Verdict as prescribed by law.

(2)19. Desecration of A Human Corpse

Any person who mutilates, defiles, or treats a deceased human body in a manner that would outrage ordinary family sensibilities commits this offense.

(2)19. Desecration of A Human Corpse is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(2)20. Illegal Possession of Human Remains

Any person who unlawfully possesses, transports, or conceals human remains without legal authorization commits this offense.

(2)20. Illegal Possession of Human Remains is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(2)21. Illegal Exhumation

Any person who unlawfully digs up, removes, or otherwise exhumes human remains from a burial site without legal authority commits illegal exhumation.

(2)21. Illegal Exhumation is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

TITLE 3. OFFENSES AGAINST PROPERTY

(3)01. Leaving Without Paying

Any person who obtains goods or services from an establishment and willfully leaves without paying the due amount commits this offense.

(3)01. Leaving Without Paying is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $300

(3)02. Petty Theft

Any person who unlawfully takes property valued below the statutory threshold (typically under $1,000) with intent to permanently deprive the owner commits petty theft.

(3)02. Petty Theft is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 7 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(3)03. Grand Theft

Any person who unlawfully takes property valued above the statutory threshold with intent to permanently deprive the owner commits grand theft.

(3)03. Grand Theft is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $6,000

(3)04. Joyriding

Any person who unlawfully takes or drives a vehicle without the owner’s consent but without intent to permanently deprive the owner commits joyriding.

(3)04. Joyriding is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 7 Months in prison with a fine of $2,500

(3)05. Grand Theft Auto

Any person who unlawfully takes a vehicle with intent to permanently deprive the owner commits grand theft auto.

(3)05. Grand Theft Auto is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 12 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(3)06. Grand Theft of Firearm

Any person who unlawfully takes possession of a firearm with intent to permanently deprive the owner commits grand theft of a firearm.

(3)06. Grand Theft of Firearm is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $25,000

(3)07. Tampering with Vehicle

Any person who unlawfully tampers with, enters, or interferes with the functioning of a vehicle without the owner’s consent commits this offense.

(3)07. Tampering with Vehicle is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $3,000

(3)08. Commercial Robbery

Any person who unlawfully takes property from another by force, fear, or intimidation commits robbery.( e.g LTD or Minimarket )

(3)08. Commercial Robbery is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $7,000

(3)10. Possession of Stolen Goods

Any person who knowingly possesses property that has been stolen commits this offense.

(3)10. Possession of Stolen Goods is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $3,500.

Peace officers who found the stolen goods will confiscate it as an evidence.

(3)11. Possession of a Stolen Identification

Any person who knowingly possesses a stolen government-issued identification document commits this offense.

(3)11. Possession of a Stolen Identification is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $7,000

(3)12. Grand Larceny Federal Reserve Banks

Any person who unlawfully takes property of high monetary value or critical importance (e.g., Pacific Standard Public Bank, County Bank, or Maze State Bank).

(3)12. Grand Larceny Federal Reserve Banks is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 50 Months in prison with a fine of $20,000

(3)13. Grand Larceny Public Reserve Banks

Any person who unlawfully takes property of high monetary value or critical importance (e.g., Flecca Public Bank, ).

(3)13. Grand Larceny Public Reserve Banks is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $10,000

(3)14. Grand Larceny Major Property Crime

Any person who unlawfully takes property of high monetary value or critical importance (e.g.,Grupee Six inc, Bobcat inc., Los Santos Cargo Stockpile, laundromart, cash exchange ).

(3)14. Grand Larceny Major Property Crime is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $10,000

(3)15. Theft of an Aircraft

Any person who unlawfully takes an aircraft without intent to permanently deprive the owner commits theft of an aircraft.

(3)15. Theft of an Aircraft is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $8,000

(3)16. Theft of a Commercial Aircraft

Any person who unlawfully takes or operates a commercial or passenger aircraft commits this offense.

(3)16. Theft of a Commercial Aircraft is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 40 Months in prison with a fine of $9,000

(3)17. Burglary

Any person who unlawfully enters a building, dwelling, or structure with intent to commit a crime therein commits burglary.

(3)17.  Burglary is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $8,000

(3)18. Trespassing

Any person who knowingly enters or remains on property without legal right or permission commits trespassing.

(3)18. Trespassing is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $1,500

(3)19. Felony Trespassing

Any person who unlawfully enters, remains upon, or gains access to restricted or secured property with the intent to commit a felony offense, or who knowingly trespasses upon designated critical infrastructure, government facilities, or other protected premises, commits the offense of Felony Trespassing.

For purposes of this section, restricted property includes, but is not limited to:

  • NOOSE Headquarters
  • Los Santos Department of Water & Power Facilities
  • Los Santos Department of Green Power Facilities
  • Los Santos Department of Nuclear Power Facilities
  • Los Santos Department of Wind Power Facilities
  • Los Santos International Airport
  • Government and Public Services Property
  • Humans Labs and Research Facilities

(3)19. Felony Trespassing is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 45 Months in prison with a fine of $90,000

(3)20. Trespassing of a Military Facility

Any person who knowingly enters or remains on a restricted military installation without authorization commits this offense.

(3)20. Trespassing of a Military Facility is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 50 Months in prison with a fine of $100,000

(3)21. Arson

Any person who willfully and maliciously sets fire to, burns, or causes to be burned any structure, forest land, or property commits arson.

(3)21. Arson is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 35 Months in prison with a fine of $50,000

(3)22. Destruction of Government Property

Any person who willfully and maliciously defaces, damages, destroys, or otherwise causes actual major physical damage to any real or personal property belonging to Government Property, without the consent or lawful authority, commits this offense.

(3)22. Destruction of Government Property is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $156,250

(3)23. Entertainment Property Taking

Any person who unlawfully takes, removes, or attempts to take property, money, or valuable items from any entertainment facility, including but not limited to casinos, theaters, concert halls, studios, or amusement venues, by means of force, threat, intimidation, or coordinated criminal action shall be guilty of Entertainment Property Taking.

(3)23. Entertainment Property Taking is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 60 Months in prison with a fine of $15,000

(3)24. Cultural Museum Property Taking

Any person who unlawfully takes, removes, damages, or attempts to take cultural, historical, or artistic property from any museum, gallery, or cultural heritage institution by means of force, threat, intimidation, or organized criminal action shall be guilty of Cultural Museum Property Taking.

This offense includes artifacts, relics, paintings, sculptures, or any item designated as cultural or historical property.

(3)24. Cultural Museum Property Taking is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 60 Months in prison with a fine of $15,000

(3)25. Government Property Taking

Any person who unlawfully takes, removes, uses, conceals, or exercises control over any government-owned property, including but not limited to official vehicles, transportation equipment, or other state assets, without lawful authority or permission, shall be guilty of Government Property Taking.

(3)25. Government Property Taking is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $5,250

(3)26. Robbery of Vangelico Property

Any person who, by means of force, violence, or intimidation, unlawfully takes precious property from the person or immediate presence of another, against the will of the lawful owner, commits a felony.

“Vangelico property” includes jewelry or articles made of gold, silver, platinum, or precious stones.

(3)26. Robbery of Vangelico Property is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $12,000

(3)27. Accessory to Robbery

Any person who, with knowledge that a robbery has been committed or is being planned, assists the perpetrator by providing transportation, scouting, or concealment, or by aiding in the disposal of stolen property, without being physically present at the immediate scene of the crime. This includes acting as a getaway driver or providing a safe haven to help the offender evade immediate capture.

(3)27. Accessory to Robbery is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of  $5,000.

(3)28. ATM Robbery

Any person who unlawfully attempts to access, damage, or extract money from an Automated Teller Machine (ATM) without authorization commits ATM Robbery.

(3)28. ATM Robbery is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 months in prison with a fine of $1,700.

(3)29. Vandalism

Any person who willfully and maliciously defaces, damages, destroys, or otherwise causes actual minor physical damage to any real or personal property belonging to another person, without the consent or lawful authority of the owner, commits this offense.

Under this section, vandalism includes, but is not limited to, graffiti, unauthorized markings, scratching, breaking, damaging, or destroying property belonging to another person, whether such property is privately or publicly owned.

(3)29. Vandalism is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 8 Months in prison with a fine of $4,500. The offender may additionally be ordered to compensate the property owner for the cost of repair, restoration, or replacement of the damaged property.

(3)30. Vandalism on Government Property

Any person who willfully and maliciously defaces, minor damages, destroys, or otherwise causes actual physical damage to any real property belonging to Government, without the consent, commits this offense.

Under this section, vandalism on Government Property includes, but is not limited to, graffiti, unauthorized markings, scratching, breaking, damaging, or destroying property belonging to Government.

(3)30. Vandalism on Government Property is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $9,000. The offender may additionally be ordered to compensate the property owner for the cost of repair, restoration, or replacement of the damaged property.

(3)31. Importation or Exportation of Stolen and Uncustomed Vehicles

Any person who steals, takes, carries away, or knowingly conceals, receives, or possesses any stolen motor vehicle within the boundaries of any port, harbor, or maritime facility knowing that such vehicle was obtained through theft, originates from an unrecorded foreign importation

(3)31. Importation or Exportation of Stolen and Uncustomed Vehicles is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 40 Months in prison with a fine of $50,000.

____________________________________________________________________________

TITLE 4. CRIMES AGAINST PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION

(4)01. Forgery

Any person who falsifies, alters, or creates a document with intent to defraud commits forgery.

(4)01. Forgery is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months  in prison with a fine of $6,500

(4)02. State Document Forgery

Any person who forges, alters, or counterfeits a state-issued document, such as IDs, licenses, or permits, commits this offense.

(4)02. State Document Forgery is categorized as a  felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months  in prison with a fine of $15,250

(4)03. Vehicle Registration Fraud

Any person who falsifies, forges, or uses counterfeit vehicle registration, plates, or titles commits vehicle registration fraud.

(4)03. Vehicle Registration Fraud is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $10,000

(4)04. Fraud

Any person who intentionally deceives another for personal gain or to cause loss to another commits fraud.

(4)04. Fraud is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(4)05. Voter Fraud

Any person who knowingly votes illegally, impersonates another voter, or manipulates election processes.

(4)05. Voter Fraud is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(4)06. Racketeering

Any person who engages in organized illegal business activities or a pattern of criminal enterprise for profit commits racketeering.

(4)06. Racketeering is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 60 Months in prison with a fine of $13,000

(4)07. Extortion

Any person who unlawfully obtains property, money, or advantage by threat, coercion, or intimidation commits extortion.

(4)07. Extortion is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 40 Months in prison with a fine of $10,000

(4)08. Money Laundering

Any person who knowingly conducts financial transactions with the proceeds of criminal activity to conceal its origin commits money laundering or has illegal money.

(4)08. Money Laundering is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of court verdict in prison with a fine of court verdict

(4)09. First Degree Possession of illegal money

Any person who knowingly possesses, holds, receives, stores, transfers, or exercises control over money or monetary instruments in an amount exceeding $400,000 that are obtained directly or indirectly from unlawful activities shall be guilty of First Degree Possession of Illegal Money.

Illegal money includes, but is not limited to, funds derived from criminal acts such as fraud, theft, embezzlement, corruption, narcotics trafficking, organized crime, money laundering, or any other offense prohibited by law.

Knowledge may be proven by direct evidence or inferred from circumstances indicating that the person knew or reasonably should have known that the money originated from illegal sources.

(4)09. First Degree Possession of Illegal Money is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(4)10. Impersonation

Any person with the act of pretending to be someone else, either in person or online, with

the intent to deceive or mislead. This title may include acts such as:Any person who falsely represents themselves as another person for gain or to cause harm commits impersonation.

(4)10. Impersonation is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $2,000

(4)11. Identity Theft

Any person who unlawfully obtains and uses the personal information of another to commit fraud or other offenses commits identity theft.

(4)11. Identity Theft is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $6,000

(4)12. Impersonating a Government Employee

Any person who falsely represents themselves as a government employee with intent to defraud or deceive commits this offense.

(4)12. Impersonating a Government Employee is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 35 Months in prison with a fine of $50,000

(4)13. Embezzlement

Any person who unlawfully appropriates property or funds entrusted to them for personal use commits embezzlement.

(4)13. Embezzlement is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $10,500

(4)14. Conspiracy

Any person who agrees with one or more persons to commit a crime and performs an overt act in furtherance of that crime commits conspiracy. This title may include acts such as:

  1. Conversations about the specifics of the offense or making a pact with other people to break the law.
  2. Getting materials or enlisting more people to join in on the plan.
  3. Actively taking part in the crime, like doing certain tasks or playing a role in the group's plan.

(4)14. Conspiracy is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict 

(4)15. Bribery

Any person who offers, gives, solicits, or accepts anything of value to influence the action of a public official commits bribery.

(4)15. Bribery is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $100,000

(4)16. Perjury

Any person who willfully makes a false statement under oath or affirmation in an official proceeding commits perjury.

(4)16. Perjury is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(4)17. Evidence Tampering

Any person who knowingly alters, destroys, or conceals evidence with intent to affect a legal proceeding commits evidence tampering

(4)17A. Evidence Tampering is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $30,000

(4)17B. or in the most severe circumstances, Court Verdict as prescribed by law.

(4)18. Witness Tampering

Any person who threatens, coerces, or offers benefit to a witness to influence testimony or prevent testimony commits witness tampering.

(4)18. Witness Tampering is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(4)19. Intimidating a Witness or Victim

Any person who threatens or harasses a witness or victim to prevent reporting or testimony commits this offense.

(4)18. Intimidating a Witness or Victim is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(4)20. Obstruction of Public Duty

Any person who knowingly hinders, delays, or obstructs a government employee performing lawful duties commits obstruction of public duty.

(4)19. Obstruction of Public Duty is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $12,000

(4)21. Obstruction of Justice

Any person who willfully interferes with law enforcement, investigations, or judicial processes commits obstruction of justice.The action can take many forms, such as:

  1. Tampering with evidence,
  2. Influencing or threatening witnesses, or
  3. Attempting to influence the outcome of a trial.

(4)21. Obstruction of Justice is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 70 Months in prison with a fine of $50,000

(4)22. Misuse of an Emergency Hotline

Any person who knowingly misuses emergency services lines for non‑emergency purposes commits this offense.

(4)22. Misuse of an Emergency Hotline is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $500

(4)23. Making a False Report of an Emergency

Any person who willfully makes a false report that triggers an emergency response commits this offense.

(4)23. Making a False Report of an Emergency is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $800

(4)24. Failure to Pay a Fine

Any person who willfully refuses to pay a lawfully imposed fine commits this offense.

(4)24. Failure to Pay a Fine is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $2,500

(4)25. Failure to Identify to a Peace Officer

Any person lawfully detained who refuses to provide accurate identification to a peace officer commits this offense.

(4)25. Failure to Identify to a Peace Officer is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $2,000

(4)26. Misdemeanor Tax Evasion

Any person who willfully fails to pay taxes in an amount under the felony threshold commits misdemeanor tax evasion.

(4)26. Misdemeanor Tax Evasion is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(4)27. Felony Tax Evasion

Any person who willfully attempts to evade taxes in an amount over the felony threshold commits felony tax evasion.

(4)27. Felony Tax Evasion is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(4)28. Gambling License Violation

Any person who conducts or participates in gambling without proper licensing commits this offense.

(4)28. Gambling License Violation is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison.

(4)29. Criminal Business Operations

Any person who operates a business for illegal purposes or as a front for criminal activity commits criminal business operations.

(4)29. Criminal Business Operations is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 150 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(4)30. Legal Practice Violation

Any person who practices law without proper license or authorization commits this offense.

(4)30. Legal Practice Violation is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of court verdict in prison with a fine of court verdict

(4)31. Medical Practice Violation

Any person who practices medicine without proper license or authorization commits this offense.

(4)31. Medical Practice Violation is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(4)32. Second Degree Possession of Illegal Money

Any person who knowingly possesses, holds, receives, stores, transfers, or exercises control over money or monetary instruments in an amount exceeding $150,000 that are obtained directly or indirectly from unlawful activities shall be guilty of Second Degree Possession of Illegal Money.

Illegal money includes, but is not limited to, funds derived from criminal acts such as fraud, theft, embezzlement, corruption, narcotics trafficking, organized crime, money laundering, or any other offense prohibited by law.

Knowledge may be proven by direct evidence or inferred from circumstances indicating that the person knew or reasonably should have known that the money originated from illegal sources.

(4)32. Second Degree Possession of Illegal Money is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 70 Months in prison with a fine of $60,000

(4)33. Third Degree Possession of Illegal Money

Any person who knowingly possesses, holds, receives, stores, transfers, or exercises control over money or monetary instruments in an amount below $149,999 that are obtained directly or indirectly from unlawful activities shall be guilty of Third Degree Possession of Illegal Money.

Illegal money includes, but is not limited to, funds derived from criminal acts such as fraud, theft, embezzlement, corruption, narcotics trafficking, organized crime, money laundering, or any other offense prohibited by law.

Knowledge may be proven by direct evidence or inferred from circumstances indicating that the person knew or reasonably should have known that the money originated from illegal sources.

(4)33. Third Degree Possession of Illegal Money is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 50 Months in prison with a fine of $35,000

(4)34. Unlawful Possession of State Insignia

Any person who knowingly possesses, wears, uses, displays, or controls any official state insignia or law enforcement identification without lawful authority shall be guilty of Unlawful Possession of State Insignia.

State insignia includes, but is not limited to, police badges, uniforms, patches, identification cards, tactical vests, or any official law enforcement or government-issued attributes. Firearms and weapons are excluded and shall be governed under separate penal code provisions.

(4)34. Unlawful Possession of State Insignia is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 12 Months in prison with a fine of $32,000

(4)35. Minor Possession of illegal money

Any person who knowingly possesses, holds, receives, stores, transfers, or exercises control over money or monetary instruments in an amount below $50,000 that are obtained directly or indirectly from unlawful activities shall be guilty of Minor Possession of Illegal Money.

Illegal money includes, but is not limited to, funds derived from criminal acts such as fraud, theft, embezzlement, corruption, narcotics trafficking, organized crime, money laundering, or any other offense prohibited by law.

Knowledge may be proven by direct evidence or inferred from circumstances indicating that the person knew or reasonably should have known that the money originated from illegal sources.

(4)35. Minor Possession of Illegal Money is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $15,000

(4)36. Third Degree Possession of Illegal Laundry Card

Any person who knowingly possesses, holds, receives, stores, transfers, or exercises control over laundry cards or monetary instruments in an amount of 10 or less that are obtained directly or indirectly from unlawful activities shall be guilty of Third Degree Possession of Illegal Laundry Credits.

Illegal laundry credits include, but are not limited to, balances derived from criminal acts such as unauthorized card reloading, hacking of machine payment systems, theft, embezzlement, or any other offense prohibited by law.

(4)36. Third Degree Possession of Illegal Laundry Cards is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $30,000

(4)37. Second Degree Possession of Illegal Laundry Cards

Any person who knowingly possesses, holds, receives, stores, transfers, or exercises control over laundry cards or monetary instruments in an amount of 39 or less cards that are obtained directly or indirectly from unlawful activities shall be guilty of Second Degree Possession of Illegal Laundry Credits.

Illegal laundry credits include, but are not limited to, balances derived from criminal acts such as unauthorized card reloading, hacking of machine payment systems, theft, embezzlement, or any other offense prohibited by law.

(4)37. Second Degree Possession of Illegal Laundry Cards is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $60,000

(4)38. First Degree Possession of Illegal Laundry Cards

Any person who knowingly possesses, holds, receives, stores, transfers, or exercises control over laundry cards or monetary instruments in an amount exceeding 40 or more  that are obtained directly or indirectly from unlawful activities shall be guilty of First Degree Possession of Illegal Laundry Credits.

Illegal laundry credits include, but are not limited to, balances derived from criminal acts such as unauthorized card reloading, hacking of machine payment systems, theft, embezzlement, or any other offense prohibited by law.

Knowledge may be proven by direct evidence or inferred from circumstances indicating that the person knew or reasonably should have known that the credits originated from illegal sources.

(4)38. First Degree Possession of Illegal Laundry Cards is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of court verdict in prison with a fine of court verdict

TITLE 5. OFFENSES AGAINST PUBLIC ORDER

(5)01. Loitering

Any person who remains in a public place without apparent purpose, after being warned by law enforcement, commits loitering.

(5)01. Loitering is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $50

(5)02. Unlawful Assembly

Any group of three or more persons who assemble with intent to commit an unlawful act, or to disturb public peace, commits unlawful assembly.

(5)02. Unlawful Assembly is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $10,000

(5)03. Incitement to Riot

Any person who encourages, promotes, or incites others to engage in riotous or violent conduct against public order commits this offense.

(5)03. Incitement to Riot is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $17,000

(5)04. Obstruction of a Government Employee

Any person who knowingly obstructs or hinders a government employee in the performance of lawful duties commits this offense.

(5)04. Obstruction of a Government Employee is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $1,500

(5)05. Disobeying a Peace Officer

Any person who willfully refuses to comply with a lawful order or direction of a peace officer commits this offense.

(5)05. Disobeying a Peace Officer is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $2,500

(5)06. Evading a Peace Officer

Any person who, with intent to evade, flees or attempts to elude a pursuing peace officer in a vehicle or on foot commits this offense.

(5)06. Evading a Peace Officer is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 6 Months in prison with a fine of $2,500

(5)07. Resisting Arrest

Any person who willfully resists, delays, or obstructs a lawful arrest by a peace officer commits resisting arrest.

(5)07. Resisting Arrest is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $1,500

(5)08. Escaping Custody

Any person who unlawfully escapes from lawful detention, jail, or custody commits this offense.

(5)08. Escaping Custody is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $3,000

(5)09. Disturbing the Peace

Any person who engages in conduct that disrupts public order, such as loud noise, fighting, or offensive language, commits disturbing the peace.

(5)09. Disturbing the Peace is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $8,000

(5)10. Failure to Appear

Any person who willfully fails to appear in court after being lawfully summoned or released on bail commits this offense.

(5)10.  Failure to Appear is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(5)11. Subpoena Violation

Any person who willfully ignores or fails to comply with a lawful subpoena commits this offense.

(5)11. Subpoena Violation is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(5)12. Violating a Court Order

Any person who knowingly disobeys a lawful court order, including restraining orders, commits this offense.

(5)12. Violating a Court Order is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(5)13. Contempt of Court

Any person who shows willful disobedience, misconduct, or disrespect toward the authority of the court commits contempt of court.

(5)13. Contempt of Court is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(5)14. Neglect of Public Duty

Any public official who willfully neglects or refuses to perform lawful duties required by their office commits neglect of public duty.

(5)14. Neglect of Public Duty is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $7,500

(5)15. Corruption of Public Office

Any public official who abuses the powers of their office for personal gain or unlawful purposes commits corruption of public office. E.g Bribery, Fraud, Extortion, Embezzlement, and Other forms of dishonesty or unlawful behavior.

(5)15. Corruption of Public Office is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.
