TITLE 6. OFFENSES AGAINST PUBLIC HEALTH  

(6)00. Misdemeanor Possession of Schedule I Controlled Substances

Any person found possessing ≤ 60 grams (3 packs or less) of a Schedule I Controlled Substance commits this offense.

(6)00. MisdemeanorPossession of Schedule I is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $2,000

(6)01. Felony Possession of Schedule I Controlled Substances

Any person found possessing ≥ 61 grams (more than 3 packs) of a Schedule I Controlled Substance commits this offense. .

(6)01. Felony Possession of Schedule I Controlled Substances is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $3,000

(6)02. Misdemeanor Possession of a Schedule II Controlled Substances

Any person found possessing ≤ 100 grams (1 pack or less) of a Schedule II Controlled Substance commits this offense.

(6)02. Misdemeanor Possession of a Schedule II Controlled Substances is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 35 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(6)03. Felony Possession of a Schedule II Controlled Substances

Any person found possessing ≥ 101 grams (more than 1 pack) of a Schedule II Controlled Substance commits this offense.

(6)02. Felony Possession of a Schedule II Controlled Substances is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 50 Months in prison with a fine of $10,000

(6)04. Drug Smuggling

Any person found possessing ≥ 2,000 grams of any scheduled controlled substance commits drug smuggling.

(6)04. Drug Smuggling is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 130 Months in prison with a fine of $50,000

(6)05. Drug Trafficking

Any person found possessing ≥ 4,000 grams of any scheduled controlled substance commits drug trafficking.

(6)05. Drug Trafficking is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(6)06. Drug Manufacturing

Any person who intentionally manufactures or attempts to manufacture a Schedule Category Controlled Substance, where such offense is established through evidence of processing, chemical synthesis, cultivation, or preparation for distribution.

(6)06. Drug Manufacturing is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(6)07. Possession of Drug Paraphernalia

Any person who knowingly and unlawfully possesses, exercises dominion or control over, or has in their custody any drug paraphernalia, with knowledge that such paraphernalia is designed for use or intended for use in unlawfully manufacturing, compounding, converting, producing, processing, preparing, injecting, ingesting, inhaling, or otherwise introducing a controlled substance into the human body, commits the offense of Possession of Drug Paraphernalia.

For purposes of this section, drug paraphernalia means all equipment, products, and materials of

any kind which are primarily designed for use or intended for use with controlled substances.

        

(6)07A. Possession of Drug Paraphernalia is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 50 Months in prison with a fine of $20,000

(6)07B. or in the most severe circumstances (≥ 10), Court Verdict as prescribed by law.

(6)08. Distribute of a Schedule Category Controlled Substances

Any person(s) found in possession of a Schedule Category Controlled Substances with Intent to Distribute with more than ≥ 800 grams.

(6)08. Distribute of a Schedule Category Controlled Substances is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 100 Months in prison with a fine of $20,000

(6)09. Drugs Selling

Any person who sells, offers to sell, a controlled substance to another person, and they possess that controlled substance is guilty for committing the offense in drug selling.

(6)09. Drugs Selling is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(6)10. Unlawful Possession of Poppy

Any person who knowingly possesses ≥ 101 kilograms of poppy without lawful authorization, permit, or exemption under applicable law commits the offense of Misdemeanor Unlawful Possession of Poppy.

Possession of 100 kilograms or less shall not constitute an offense under this section. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any person found in possession of 100 kilograms or less of poppy in conjunction with any controlled substance, narcotic, drug manufacturing materials, drug packaging materials, distribution paraphernalia, or other drug-related paraphernalia shall be deemed to possess the poppy as evidence of unlawful drug activity and may be detained and charged with the applicable offense of Drug Paraphernalia Possession or any other applicable controlled substance offense, as supported by the totality of the circumstances.

(6)10. Unlawful Possession of Poppy is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(6)11. Felony Possession of Poppy

Any person who knowingly possesses ≥ 200 kilograms of poppy but not exceeding 300 kilograms of poppy without lawful authorization, permit, or exemption under applicable law commits the offense of Felony Unlawful Possession of Poppy.

(6)11. Felony Possession of Poppy is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 80 Months in prison with a fine of $15,000

(6)12. Aggravated Possession of Poppy

Any person who knowingly possesses ≥ 301 kilograms of poppy without lawful authorization, permit, or exemption under applicable law commits the offense of Aggravated Felony Possession of Poppy.

(6)12. Aggravated Possession of Poppy is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

TITLE 7. CRIMES AGAINST PUBLIC SAFETY AND SECURITY  

(7)01. Possession of an Unlicensed Firearm [Class 1]

The act of possessing or carrying a Class 1 firearm (such as a standard pistol or handgun) without proper state issued licensing or permits.

(7)02. Possession of an Unlicensed Firearm [Class 1] is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $1,000

(7)02. Possession of an Unlicensed Firearm [Class 2]

The act of possessing or carrying a Class 2 firearm (such as a shotgun or rifle) without proper licensing or permits.

(7)02. Possession of an Unlicensed Firearm [Class 2] is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 50 Months in prison with a fine of $10,000

(7)03. Criminal Possession of a Firearm [Class 1] 

Unlawful possession of a Class 1 firearm by a prohibited individual, such as a convicted felon or someone under legal firearm restrictions. Ex;  Pistol .50, ceramic pistol, X17, machine Pistol, ST84 Skulln Sword, MX18 Classyblue

(7)03. Criminal Possession of a Firearm [Class 1] is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 12 Months in prison with a fine of $1,200

(7)04. Criminal Possession of a Firearm [Class 2]

Possessing a Class 2 firearm during the commission of a crime, while under probation/parole, or with criminal intent. Ex; Mini SMG, Micro SMG, SMG, Navy Revolver, KVR, Pump Shotgun, Revolver black Sawn Of Shotgun, SDR,7 VTN33 Graveshift,

(7)04. Criminal Possession of a Firearm [Class 2] is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 45 Months in prison with a fine of $30,600

(7)05. Criminal Possession of a Firearm [Class 3]

Possession of a Class 3 firearm, including automatic weapons or other military-grade firearms, without federal clearance or in violation of law. Ex ; Double Action, Assault Rifle, Carbine Rifle, MB47, AGC, BK12, Dragon Scarl, Godzilla, AK47, Purplefunk AKT ,Foolv2 RED, M6A9 Diamond Soul,Scarl Rusty, M4 T Neon Integrale

(7)05. Criminal Possession of a Firearm [Class 3] is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 60 Months in prison with a fine of $85,000

(7)06. Criminal Possession of a Government-Issue Firearm

Unlawful possession of a firearm issued specifically to law enforcement or military personnel, without authorization.

(7)06. Criminal Possession of a Government-Issue Firearm is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 100 Months in prison with a fine of $30,000

(7)07. Criminal Possession of a Government Issued Baton 

Illegal possession of a law enforcement-issued baton, typically restricted for official duty use.

(7)07. Criminal Possession of a Government Issued Baton is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $200

(7)08. Criminal Possession of a Government Issued Taser

Illegal possession or use of a stun gun or taser meant solely for government or law enforcement use.

(7)08. Criminal Possession of a Government Issued Taser is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $1,000

(7)09. Possession of Unauthorized Device

Possessing or utilizing unauthorized hardware/software to bypass government restrictions, surveillance, or enforcement systems.

(7)09. Possession of Unauthorized Device is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $1,000

(7)10. Possession of Destructive Devices

Possessing items such as pipe bombs, grenades, or other devices classified as destructive weapons under state law and federal law.

(7)10. Possession of Destructive Devices is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 10 in prison with a fine of $800

(7)10. Possession of Destructive Devices if has pipe bombs, grenades or military grade is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(7)11. Criminal Use of Explosives

Possessing or using explosive materials (e.g., dynamite, grenades, pipe bombs) with intent to cause damage or fear constitutes criminal use of explosives.

(7)11. Criminal Use of Explosives is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $20,000

(7)12. Misdemeanor Possession of Thermite Charge

Possessing a small amount of thermite or a thermite charge, not intended for malicious use, constitutes misdemeanor possession.

(7)12. Misdemeanor Possession of Thermite Charge is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $5,500

(7)13. Felony Possession of Thermite Charge

Possessing thermite or a thermite charge with intent to use it unlawfully or cause significant damage.

(7)13. Felony Possession of Thermite Charge is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $12,000

(7)14. Failure to Report A Stolen Firearm

Failing to notify law enforcement when aware of the theft or loss of a firearm.

(7)14. Failure To Report A Stolen Firearm is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $3,000

(7)15. Criminal Use of a Firearm

Discharging or using a firearm in a criminal act, whether an assault or during another felony.

(7)15. Criminal Use of a Firearm is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 8 Months in prison with a fine of $1,500

(7)16. Brandishing of a Firearm

Displaying or exhibiting a firearm in a threatening or reckless manner in public, without lawful justification.

(7)16. Brandishing of a Firearm is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 7 Months in prison with a fine of $4,500

(7)17. Brandishing non Firearm

Threatening another with a weapon that is not a firearm (e.g., knife, blunt object) in a threatening way.

(7)17. Brandishing non Firearm is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $2,000

(7)18. Weapon Discharge Violation

Discharging any weapon in an unsafe location or manner not justified by self-defense or threat mitigation.

(7)18. Weapons Discharge Violation is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(7)19. Unlawful Possession of Ammunition

Possessing ammunition (300 Ammo) without proper licensing (even if not carrying a weapon) is unlawful.

(7)19. Unlawful Possession of Ammunition is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $345

(7)20. Illegal Distribution of Ammunition

Selling, possessing, giving away, or otherwise distributing ammunition without proper authorization or licensing if less than 2000 Ammo

(7)20. Illegal Distribution of Ammunition is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 12 Months in prison with a fine of $1,460

(7)21. First Degree Criminal Sale of a Legalized Firearm [Class 1]

Sale regulated firearms [Class 1 ] without license, who has been caught selling up to 10 legalized firearms will be punished by this title.

(7)21. First Degree Criminal Sale of a Legalized Firearm [Class 1] is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 60 Months in prison with a fine of $12,250

(7)22. Second Degree Criminal Sale of a Legalized Firearm [Class1]

Sale regulated firearms [Class 1 ] without license, who has been caught selling up to 5 legalized firearms will be punished by this title.

(7)22. Second Degree Criminal Sale of a Legalized Firearm [Class1] is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 40 Months in prison with a fine of $8,250

(7)23. Third Degree Criminal Sale of Legalized Firearm [Class 1]

Sale regulated firearms [Class 1 ] without license, who has been caught selling up to 2 legalized firearms will be punished by this title.

(7)23. Third Degree Criminal Sale of Legalized Firearm [Class 1] is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $4,750

(7)27. First Degree Criminal Sale of Government Issued Firearm

Sale regulated Government firearms, who have been caught selling up to 10 legalized firearms will be punished by this title.

(7)27. First Degree Criminal Sale of Government Issued Firearm is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 150 Months in prison with a fine of $60,000

(7)28. Second Degree Criminal Sale of Government Issued Firearm

Sale regulated Government firearms, who have been caught selling up to 5 legalized firearms will be punished by this title.

(7)28. Second Degree Criminal Sale of Government Issued Firearm is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 120 Months in prison with a fine of $40,000

(7)29. Third Degree Criminal Sale of Government Issued Firearm

Sale regulated Government firearms, who have been caught selling up to 2 legalized firearms will be punished by this title.

(7)29. Third Degree Criminal Sale of Government Issued Firearm is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 80 Months in prison with a fine of $20,000

(7)30. Criminal Sale of an Illegal Weapon nor Destructive Devices

Selling prohibited weapons, explosives, or destructive devices without authorization.

(7)30. Criminal Sale of an Illegal Weapon nor Destructive Devices is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 120 Months in prison with a fine of $50.000

(7)31. Manufacture of an Illegal Weapon or Destructive Devices

Designing, creating, or fabricating prohibited weapons or destructive devices.

(7)31. Manufacture of a Destructive Device or Prohibited Weapon is categorized as a felony and is punishable by Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(7)32. Flying into Restricted Airspace

Operating or piloting an aircraft into military or restricted zones without clearance or authorization.

(7)32. Flying into Restricted Airspace is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $1,000

(7)33. Piloting Without a Proper License

Operating any aircraft without having the required pilots' certification.

(7)33. Piloting Without a Proper License is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $500

(7)34. Vigilantism

Taking law enforcement into one’s own hands, using force or pursuing suspects without legal authority.

(7)34. Vigilantism is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $200

(7)35. Jaywalking

Crossing a roadway outside designated crosswalks or against signal systems.

(7)35. Jaywalking is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable with a fine of $50

(7)36. Weapon Smuggling

Any person found in possession of more than eight (8) weapons commits weapon smuggling. May be determined by:
• Quantity of weapons
• Moving weapons to gangs/organizations
• Delivering shipment drops

• Presence of weapon attachments in bulk more than 40.

• Packaging materials or storage crates

(7)36. Weapon Smuggling is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(7)37. Eavesdropping

Using electronic or mechanical means to secretly listen in on private conversations for unlawful purposes.

(7)37. Eavesdropping is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 8 Months in prison with a fine of $875

(7)38. Attempted Prison Break

Trying to escape from lawful incarceration without success.

(7)38. Attempted Prison Break  is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $800

(7)39. Prison Break 

Successfully escaping from jail or detention.

(7)39. Prison Break is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 40 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(7)40. Accessory to Prison Break

Assisting in or facilitating the escape of someone from lawful custody.

(7)40. Accessory to Prison Break is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 35 Months in prison with a fine of $2,000

(7)41. Harboring Fugitive

Providing shelter, assistance, or concealment to an individual known to be evading arrest.

(7)41. Harboring Fugitive is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term Court Verdict or in the most severe circumstances, the Death Sentence as prescribed by law.

(7)42. Drive-By Shooting

Firing a firearm from a moving vehicle at people, houses, or occupied spaces.

(7)42. Drive-By Shooting is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $1,250

(7)43. Misdemeanor Possession of Bulletproof Vest

Any person who knowingly possesses, owns, carries, or controls a bulletproof vest or body armor without lawful authorization, or while not acting in an official capacity as a member of law enforcement, military, or other authorized government agency, shall be guilty of unlawful possession of protective equipment less than 10.

(7)43. Misdemeanor Possession of Bulletproof Vest is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $3,280

(7)44. Felony Possession of Bulletproof Vest

Any person who knowingly possesses, owns, carries, or controls a bulletproof vest or body armor without lawful authorization, or while not acting in an official capacity as a member of law enforcement, military, or other authorized government agency, shall be guilty of unlawful possession of protective equipment more than 10.

(7)44. Felony Possession of Bulletproof Vest is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(7)45. Misdemeanor Unlawful Possession of Weapon component

Any person who knowingly possesses fewer than twenty (20) prohibited weapon components without lawful permit or authorization shall be guilty of a misdemeanor offense of Unlawful Possession of a Weapon Component.

(7)45. Misdemeanor Unlawful Possession of Weapon component is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(7)46. Felony Unlawful Possession of Weapon component

Any person who knowingly possesses more than twenty (20) units of any prohibited or controlled weapon component, without lawful authorization, commits the offense of Felony Unlawful Possession of a Weapon Component.

(7)46. Felony Unlawful Possession of Weapon component is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $7,000

(7)47. Manufacturing  of Weapon component

Any person who knowingly manufactures, fabricates, assembles, or produces any prohibited or controlled weapon component without lawful authorization commits the offense of Felony Unlawful Manufacturing of a Weapon Component.

(7)47. Manufacturing of Weapon component is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(7)48. Ammunition Smuggling

Any person found in possession of more than 2000 Ammo commits Ammunition Smuggling

May be determined by:
• Quantity of Ammunitions
• Moving Ammunitions to gangs/organizations
• Delivering shipment drops

• Presence of Ammunition in bulk

• Packaging materials or storage crates

(7)48. Ammunition Smuggling is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of Court Verdict in prison with a fine of Court Verdict

(7)49. Usage of Suppressor 

Any person who knowingly uses, attaches, equips, or discharges a firearm fitted with a suppressor without lawful authorization commits the offense of Felony Unlawful Usage of a Suppressor.

(7)49. Usage of Suppressor is categorized as a Felony and is punishable by 20 months imprisonment with a fine of  $5,000.

TITLE 8. CRIMES AGAINST THE TRAFFIC OPERATION

(8)01. Vehicle  Registration Violation

Failing to display a valid license plate or current registration tags, or using falsified registration documents.

(8)01. Vehicle Registration Violation is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $30,000

(8)02. Hit and Run

Leaving the scene after causing property damage or injury in a vehicular accident without providing identification or rendering aid when legally required.

(8)02. Hit and Run is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 30 Months in prison with a fine of $1,000

(8)04. Evading Peace Officer on Aircraft

Using an aircraft to evade law enforcement direction or pursuit.

(8)04. Evading Peace Officer on Aircraft is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $1,500

(8)05. Unsafe Usage of a Bicycle

Operating a bicycle in a reckless manner that endangers pedestrians or other road users, without following safety regulations (e.g., riding against traffic).

(8)05. Unsafe Usage of a Bicycle is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $250

(8)06. Reckless Driving

Operating a vehicle with willful disregard for the safety of persons or property.

(8)06. Reckless Driving is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $500

(8)07. Failure to Present Identification ( Traffic )

Operating a motor vehicle without physically carrying a valid identification card or driver's license, or failing to present it to law enforcement upon lawful request.

(8)07. Failure to Present Identification ( Traffic )  is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $200

(8)08. Reckless Evading of a Peace Officer

Evading law enforcement in a manner that demonstrates willful or wanton disregard for safety (e.g., driving at extremely high speed or weaving through traffic).

(8)08. Reckless Evading of a Peace Officer is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $15,000

(8)09. Aerial Evasion

Evasion of law enforcement via aircraft, drone, or other air-based means, endangering public safety.

(8)09. Aerial Evasion is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 10 Months in prison with a fine of $800

(8)10. Riding on a Sidewalk

Operating a motor vehicle or bicycle on a sidewalk in a manner that is unsafe or not permitted.

(8)10. Riding on a Sidewalk is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $100

(8)11. Illegal Passing

Passing another vehicle in a no-passing zone or head-on without proper visibility or signals.

(8)11. Illegal Passing is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $150

(8)12. Illegal Turn

Making an unpermitted or unsafe turn (e.g., U-turn at prohibited location) that endangers others.

(8)12. Illegal Turn is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $150

(8)13.  Driving on the Wrong Side of the Road

Operating a vehicle against traffic flow on a two-way road.

(8)13. Driving on the Wrong Side of the Road is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $100

(8)14. Negligent Operation of a Vehicle 

Operating a vehicle without due care or attention to traffic laws, causing a potential hazard.

(8)14. Negligent Operation of a Vehicle is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $100

(8)15. Yield Violation

Failing to yield right-of-way when required by law, such as at stop signs or pedestrian crossings.

(8)15. Yield Violation is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $25

(8)16. Failure to Obey Traffic Control Devices

Ignoring traffic signals, stop signs, or road markings designated for orderly vehicle control.

(8)16. Failure to Obey Traffic Control Devices is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $100

(8)17. Failure to Yield to Emergency Vehicle  

Not pulling over or yielding right-of-way to police, fire, or ambulance when lights/sirens are active.

(8)17. Failure to Yield to Emergency Vehicle is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $100

(8)18. Unauthorized Parking

Parking in restricted areas (e.g., fire lanes, handicapped spots) without proper permission.

(8)18. Unauthorized Parking is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $75

(8)19. Third Degree Speeding

Exceeding posted speed limits by 61 KMH - 80 KMH.

(8)19. Third Degree Speeding is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $300

(8)20. Second Degree Speeding

Exceeding posted speed limits by 81 KMH - 120 KMH.

(8)20. Second Degree Speeding is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $500

(8)21. First Degree Speeding

Exceeding posted speed limits by 121 KMH - 260 KMH.

(8)21. First Degree Speeding is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $600

(8)22. Driving Without a Valid License

Operating a vehicle without a currently valid driver's license.

(8)22. Driving Without a Valid License is categorized as an infraction and is punishable  with a fine of $200

(8)23. Driving While Intoxicated

Operating a vehicle under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances beyond legal limits.

(8)24. Driving While Intoxicated is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable  with a fine of $250

(8)24. Driving Under the Influence

General offense for impaired driving due to drugs (including prescription or controlled substances).

(8)25. Driving under the Influence is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 12 Months in prison with a fine of $700

(8)25. Driving Without Use of Headlights

Operating a vehicle at night or in low visibility without using headlights as required.

(8)25. Driving Without Use of Headlights is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $150

(8)26. Operating an Unsafe Vehicle

Driving a vehicle that is not roadworthy due to mechanical defects thus endangering public safety.

(8)26. Operating an Unsafe Vehicle is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 5 Months in prison with a fine of $200

(8)27. Tinted Windows

Using window tint beyond legal limit 30 %, restricting visibility for enforcement or safety.

(8)27. Tinted Windows is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $250

(8)28. Vehicular Noise Violation

Operating a vehicle with excessively loud modifications (e.g. mufflers or exhausts) beyond permissible decibel levels.

(8)28. Vehicular Noise Violation is categorized as an infraction and is punishable with a fine of $500

(8)29. Unauthorized Speed Contests

Organizing or participating in street racing or speed competitions on public roads.

(8)29. Unauthorized Speed Contests is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 8 Months in prison with a fine of $10,000

(8)30. Street Racing

Actively participating in illegal races between vehicles on public streets.

(8)30. Street Racing is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 35 Months in prison with a fine of $15,000

(8)31. Possession of Nitrous Oxide

Holding nitrous oxide canisters intended for automotive performance enhancement without proper authorization.

(8)31. Possession of Nitrous Oxide is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $2,500

(8)32. Use of Nitrous Oxide

Activating or using nitrous oxide injection systems in a vehicle illegally during operation.

(8)32. Use Of Nitrous Oxide is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 22 Months in prison with a fine of $2,700

(8)33. Unlawful Possession of an Illegal Racing Device

Any person who knowingly possesses, installs, or distributes any prohibited electronic or mechanical device designed to bypass factory speed limiters, manipulate for street racing, or interfere with traffic control.

(8)33. Unlawful Possession of an Illegal Racing Device is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in jail with a fine of $1,570

(8)34. Failure to Use Required Safety Equipment

Any person who operates or rides in a motor vehicle on a public roadway while failing to use the required safety equipment required by law, including but not limited to a protective helmet, and/or seat belt, commits this offense.

(8)34. Failure to Use Required Safety Equipment is categorized as an infraction and is punishable by a fine of $400

(8)35. Misdemeanor Instrumentality of a Crime

Any person who knowingly uses, permits the use of, or provides any vehicle, vessel, or personal property as an instrumentality to facilitate, aid, or abet the commission of fewer than three (3)

(8)35. Misdemeanor Instrumentality of a Crime is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in jail with a fine of $20,000

(8)36. Felony Instrumentality of a Crime

Any person who knowingly uses, permits the use of, or provides any vehicle, vessel, or personal property as an instrumentality to facilitate, aid, or abet the commission of three (3) or more

(8)36. Felony Instrumentality of a Crime is categorized as a felony and is punishable by a term of 40 Months in jail with a fine of $35,000

TITLE 9. PARKS AND WILDLIFE CODE

(9)01. Hunting in an Unregulated Area

Hunting outside of the Hunting Area/Zone as designated by the State of San Andreas. Offenders are subject to search for any animals or animal parts acquired by hunting outside of the designated hunting area/zone. After three or more offenses, individuals are subject to removal of their Hunting License.

(9)01. Hunting in an Unregulated Area is categorized as an infraction and is punishable by a term of 10 in prison with a fine of $600

(9)02. Poaching

No person shall either individually or in association with one or more other persons, willfully bait, trap, hunt, injure, maim, kill, or otherwise harm any animal named on the restricted hunting or fishing lists maintained by the State including:

Blue Shark,

Lake Strurgeon

Tiger Shark

Sea Turtle

Hammerhead Shark

Blacktip Reef Shark

Pink River Dolphin

Paddlefish

Sawfish

Lion

(9)02. Poaching is categorized as a Felony and is punishable by a term of 20 Months in prison with a fine of $10,000

(9)03. Hunting/Fishing Without a License

Hunting/Fishing in a public area without proper licensure issued by the State. All illegally obtained carcasses are to be confiscated and destroyed in accordance with Park Ranger SOPs.

(9)03. Hunting/Fishing Without a License is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $5,000

(9)04. Animal Cruelty

Intentionally inflicting harm, suffering, or death upon an animal through abuse, neglect, torture, abandonment, or failure to provide necessary sustenance, medical care, or shelter. This also includes animal fighting (e.g., dogfighting, cockfighting), poisoning animals, or performing cruel experiments without lawful exemption.

(9)04A. Animal Cruelty is categorized as a misdemeanor and is punishable by a term of 15 Months in prison with a fine of $1,500

(9)04B. Animal Cruelty intentional torture, repeated abuse, organized fighting, or acts resulting in severe injury or death of the animal is categorized as a Felony and is punishable by a term of 25 Months in prison with a fine of $3,000

TITLE 10. SENTENCING ENHANCEMENTS

Description:

Sentencing enhancements are legal provisions that allow a court to impose a punishment greater than the standard statutory penalty for an offense when specific aggravating circumstances are proven. These enhancements operate in addition to the base sentence and are intended to reflect the increased severity, danger, or social harm of the conduct. They may apply to both misdemeanor and felony offenses, but are most commonly associated with serious felonies.

Purpose:
The purpose of sentencing enhancements is to:

  1. Address situations where the offense is committed under circumstances that demonstrate greater culpability or potential for harm.
    Provide a deterrent effect by imposing harsher penalties for particularly dangerous or harmful conduct.
  2. Ensure that repeat offenders or those committing crimes with aggravating factors receive longer periods of incarceration or higher fines.

Application in Court:
Sentencing enhancements must be formally alleged by the prosecution, usually in the charging document, and must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt unless the defendant admits them in a plea agreement. If proven, the enhancement is added to the sentence for the underlying offense. In some jurisdictions, these enhancements carry mandatory minimum sentences that cannot be reduced by parole, probation, or other forms of early release.

Legal Effect:
When a sentencing enhancement applies, the court increases the defendant’s sentence above the base statutory range for the offense. This can be done in various ways depending on the jurisdiction:

  1. Adding a fixed number of years to the prison term.
  2. Increasing the minimum and/or maximum term of imprisonment.
  3. Elevating the classification of the offense (e.g., from misdemeanor to felony).
  4. Imposing mandatory consecutive sentences rather than allowing concurrent terms.

____________________________________________________________________________

TITLE 11. PEACE OFFICER

Definition:
A Peace Officer is a person who is legally designated and authorized by law to enforce statutes, maintain public order, prevent and detect crime, and protect life and property. The term is broader than “police officer” and encompasses a range of law enforcement roles as defined by each jurisdiction’s statutes.

Scope of Authority:
Peace Officers derive their authority from state or local law and may exercise powers of arrest, search, seizure, and detention. Their jurisdiction can vary depending on their appointment some have statewide authority, while others are limited to specific municipalities, agencies, or functions.

Examples of Peace Officers:
 Depending on jurisdiction, Peace Officers may include:

  1. Los Santos Police Department
  2. Los Santos Sheriff Department
  3. San Andreas State Police

Court Relevance:

The classification of an individual as a peace officer is legally significant. Certain offenses such as assaulting, resisting, or obstructing a peace officer carry enhanced penalties due to the victim’s status. Additionally, some statutes grant peace officers special procedural protections, evidentiary privileges, and powers in the execution of their duties.

____________________________________________________________________________

TITLE 12. CITIZEN DETAINMENT PROCEDURES

Description:

Regulates in a strict and limited manner the authority of private persons to temporarily detain another individual, including the conditions, manner, and purpose of such detainment.

Purpose:

Ensures that citizen detainment is conducted solely for legitimate law-enforcement purposes and prevents arbitrary actions or violations of individual rights.

Application in Court:

Applied by courts to assess the legality, reasonableness, and criminal or civil liability arising from detainment conducted by private persons.

PREAMBLE: Policy and Guidelines

Purpose

San Andreas Penal Code berfungsi sebagai kerangka hukum utama yang mengatur tindakan kriminal, prosedur penegakan hukum, dan sanksi di dalam yurisdiksi State of San Andreas. Dokumen ini merangkum kebijakan dan guidelines yang dirancang untuk menjamin keadilan, menjaga ketertiban umum, dan menjunjung tinggi hak-hak konstitusional.

______________________________________________________________________________

DEFINITIONS

CHAPTER 1 GENERAL PURPOSE

The main objectives of this chapter are to:

  1. Menetapkan prinsip-prinsip dasar dari San Andreas Penal Code.

  2. Mendefinisikan tujuan dan ruang lingkup penegakan hukum pidana di dalam negara bagian.

  3. Memberikan panduan yang jelas bagi law enforcement officers, jaksa, dan otoritas yudisial dalam penerapan hukum negara.

  4. Menjamin konsistensi dan keadilan dalam proses pidana serta administrasi peradilan.

  5. Melindungi hak dan keselamatan seluruh warga, pendatang, dan entitas di dalam San Andreas.

  6. Meningkatkan ketertiban umum dan efek jera (deterrence), mengurangi tingkat kejahatan melalui kerangka hukum yang transparan dan terukur.

  7. Mendukung tujuan legislatif dalam menjaga masyarakat yang lawful, aman, dan adil.

CHAPTER 2 GENERAL DEFINITIONS

Section 2.1 – Person

  • "Person" mencakup setiap individu, warga negara, pengunjung, atau penduduk di dalam yurisdiksi San Andreas.
  • Istilah ini juga mencakup entitas hukum seperti korporasi, kemitraan, dan asosiasi, kecuali konteksnya menentukan lain.

Section 2.2 – Law Enforcement Officer

  • Seorang "Law Enforcement Officer" adalah individu mana pun yang secara resmi diberikan wewenang untuk menegakkan hukum di San Andreas.
  • Ini mencakup:
  1. Police Officers dan Deputies dari yurisdiksi lokal atau wilayah (county).
  2. State Troopers atau Highway Patrol Officers.
  3. Petugas resmi lainnya yang secara hukum berwenang untuk melakukan penangkapan dan menjaga ketertiban umum.

Section 2.3 – Government employee

  • "Government employee" merujuk pada karyawan mana pun yang sedang bertugas (on-duty) di instansi pemerintah tingkat lokal, negara bagian, atau federal.

Section 2.4 – Offense

  • Sebuah "Offense" adalah tindakan atau kelalaian apa pun yang dilarang oleh San Andreas Penal Code atau hukum lain yang berlaku, dan dapat dihukum dengan denda, penjara, atau sanksi lainnya.

Section 2.5 – Felony

  • Felony adalah tindak pidana serius yang dapat dihukum lebih dari satu tahun penjara, denda dalam jumlah besar, atau keduanya.

Section 2.6 – Misdemeanor

  • Misdemeanor adalah tindak pidana yang tingkatnya lebih ringan, yang dapat dihukum hingga satu tahun penjara, denda, atau keduanya.

Section 2.7 – Infraction

  • Infraction adalah pelanggaran hukum ringan yang tidak dapat dihukum dengan hukuman penjara.
  • Infractions biasanya berujung pada denda, peringatan, atau sanksi administratif.

Section 2.8 – Attempt

  • Attempt (Percobaan) terjadi ketika seseorang berniat untuk melakukan suatu pelanggaran (offense) dan mengambil langkah nyata menuju hal tersebut, meskipun kejahatan tersebut tidak sampai selesai/terjadi.

Section 2.9 – Accomplice

  • Accomplice (Kaki tangan) adalah setiap orang yang dengan sengaja membantu, memfasilitasi, atau mendorong individu lain untuk melakukan suatu pelanggaran (offense).

Section 3.0 – Weapon

  • Sebuah "Weapon" didefinisikan sebagai objek, alat, instrumen, atau zat apa pun yang dirancang, dibuat, atau dimodifikasi dengan tujuan utama untuk menyebabkan kematian atau cedera tubuh yang serius, atau digunakan/dimaksudkan untuk digunakan dengan cara yang dapat menyebabkan kematian, cedera serius, atau penghancuran properti, baik yang mematikan (lethal) maupun tidak (non-lethal). Ada tiga tipe klasifikasi senjata:

Class 1

Kategori: Senjata yang umum dimiliki oleh warga sipil dengan tingkat risiko sedang. Umumnya legal untuk dimiliki, baik dengan maupun tanpa lisensi standar tergantung pada regulasi yang berlaku.

  • Contoh Senjata: Pistol .50, Ceramic Pistol, X17, Machine Pistol, ST84 Skulln Sword, MX18 Classyblue.

Class 2

Kategori: Senjata dengan tingkat mematikan yang lebih tinggi atau memiliki kemampuan menembak cepat (rapid-fire). Kelompok ini mencakup senjata laras pendek otomatis dan senapan sebar.

  • Contoh Senjata: Mini SMG, Micro SMG, SMG, Navy Revolver, KVR, Pump Shotgun, Revolver Black Swan, Sawed-Off Shotgun, SDR, VTN33 Graveshift.

Class 3

Kategori: Senjata yang ditujukan untuk penggunaan militer, sangat mematikan, atau memiliki potensi kehancuran massal. Kelompok ini mencakup senapan serbu (assault rifle) dan senjata berat lainnya.

  • Contoh Senjata: Double Action, Assault Rifle, Carbine Rifle, MB47, AGC, BK12, Dragon Scarl, Godzilla, AK47, Purplefunk AKT, Foolv2 RED, M6A9 Diamond Soul, Scarl Rusty, M4 T Neon Integrale.

  • Sebuah "firearm", yang juga sering disebut sebagai "gun", adalah senjata apa pun yang dirancang untuk melontarkan proyektil melalui kekuatan ledakan atau pembakaran, dan mampu menyebabkan kematian atau cedera serius.

Section 3.2 – Machine Gun

  • Sebuah machine gun adalah tipe senjata api yang mampu menembak secara fully automatic, artinya dapat mengeluarkan banyak peluru secara terus-menerus hanya dengan satu kali tarikan pelatuk (trigger) sampai pelatuk dilepas, amunisi habis, atau senjata mengalami malfungsi. Berbeda dengan senjata api semi-automatic yang hanya menembakkan satu peluru per tarikan pelatuk, sebuah machine gun dirancang khusus untuk tembakan cepat dan berkelanjutan, menjadikannya jauh lebih mematikan dan berbahaya baik untuk penggunaan ofensif maupun defensif. Di bawah hukum negara bagian dan federal, machine guns sangat dibatasi atau dilarang untuk kepemilikan sipil karena kapasitasnya yang dapat menyebabkan bahaya massal. Kepemilikan, penjualan, atau pemindahan tanpa otorisasi/lisensi yang tepat biasanya diklasifikasikan sebagai pelanggaran serious felony.

Section 3.3 – Destructive Devices

  • Sebuah destructive device adalah senjata peledak, pembakar (incendiary), atau kimia apa pun yang dirancang untuk menyebabkan kerusakan properti yang signifikan, cedera, atau kematian; termasuk namun tidak terbatas pada bom, granat, roket, rudal, ranjau, bom Molotov, dan alat serupa lainnya yang mampu melakukan penghancuran massal. Definisi ini juga mencakup senjata api atau peluncur apa pun dengan diameter laras (bore) lebih dari setengah inci yang tidak dianggap cocok untuk tujuan olahraga, serta kombinasi komponen apa pun yang dimaksudkan untuk merakit alat tersebut. Destructive devices sangat dilarang di bawah hukum negara bagian dan federal. Kepemilikan, pembuatan, penjualan, atau penggunaan tanpa izin atas alat-alat ini merupakan tindakan serious felony karena ancaman ekstrem yang ditimbulkan terhadap keamanan publik.

Section 3.4 – MDT

  • MDT singkatan dari Mobile Data Terminal. Ini adalah sistem komputer portabel atau yang dipasang di kendaraan yang memungkinkan police officers, emergency responders, atau agen pemerintah untuk mengakses dan input data langsung ke database instansi mereka secara real time.

Section 3.5 – HUT

  • Hold Until Trial (HUT) adalah status penahanan pre-trial di mana seorang tersangka tetap berada dalam tahanan sampai jadwal persidangan atau court hearing mereka. Hal ini dilakukan karena tingkat keparahan pelanggaran atau risiko yang mereka timbulkan terhadap keselamatan publik. Seorang tersangka bisa ditahan dengan status HUT jika dianggap sebagai flight risk (berisiko kabur), kemungkinan besar akan melakukan kejahatan lagi, atau membahayakan masyarakat maupun saksi-saksi.

Section 3.6 – Serious Body Harm

  • Serious Bodily Harm adalah cedera fisik apa pun yang menimbulkan risiko kematian yang besar, menyebabkan cacat jangka panjang atau permanen, mengakibatkan kehilangan atau gangguan fungsi anggota tubuh atau organ secara signifikan, atau membutuhkan perawatan medis intensif/rawat inap. Cedera yang termasuk dalam kategori ini meliputi patah tulang parah, luka robek yang dalam (deep lacerations), luka bakar parah, atau kerusakan organ dalam. Level cedera ini biasanya dikaitkan dengan aggravated offenses (pelanggaran berat) dan dapat menaikkan status kejahatan menjadi felony atau kelas hukuman yang lebih tinggi.

Section 3.7 – Controlled Substance

  • Controlled Substance adalah obat-obatan, bahan kimia, atau zat apa pun yang pembuatan, kepemilikan, distribusi, atau penggunaannya diatur oleh hukum. Zat ini diklasifikasikan ke dalam schedule atau kategori tertentu berdasarkan nilai medisnya, potensi penyalahgunaan, dan risiko terhadap kesehatan publik. Ada tiga tipe Controlled Substance di Negara Bagian San Andreas:
  • Schedule I: Weed bag / Cannabis / Marijuana.
  • Schedule II: Methamphetamine, Cocaine.
  • Schedule III: Saat ini belum diketahui, perlu dicek lebih lanjut di laboratorium.

CHAPTER 3 CRIMINAL TERM DEFINITIONS

  • “Contraband” – Barang apa pun yang ilegal untuk dimiliki, diangkut, atau didistribusikan menurut hukum.
  • “Deadly Force” – Berarti kekuatan yang mampu menyebabkan kematian atau cedera tubuh serius, termasuk penggunaan senjata api atau senjata mematikan lainnya.
  • “Detention” – Berarti tindakan menahan seseorang secara sah dalam pengawasan (custody) atau membatasi kebebasan bergerak mereka untuk tujuan investigasi atau perlindungan.
  • “Arrest” – Menggunakan otoritas hukum untuk membawa seseorang ke dalam tahanan. Sebuah arrest umumnya dilakukan ketika ada probable cause bahwa individu tersebut telah melakukan kejahatan.
  • “Force” – Kekuatan, kekerasan, atau tekanan yang diberikan terhadap seseorang atau benda untuk memaksa kepatuhan atau mengatasi perlawanan (resistance).
  • “Malice Aforethought” – Keputusan sadar dan sengaja untuk melakukan tindakan yang diketahui oleh pelaku sebagai tindakan melawan hukum dan kemungkinan besar akan menyebabkan bahaya.
  • “Risk” – Potensi bahaya, ancaman, atau kemungkinan terjadinya kerugian atau kerusakan yang diakibatkan oleh suatu tindakan atau situasi.
  • “Probable Cause” – Dasar atau alasan yang masuk akal berdasarkan fakta dan keadaan yang akan membuat orang yang bijaksana percaya bahwa suatu kejahatan telah atau sedang dilakukan.
  • “Accessory” – Seseorang yang membantu, menolong, atau memfasilitasi orang lain dalam melakukan kejahatan, baik sebelum maupun sesudah kejadian (before or after the fact).

CHAPTER 4 GOVERNMENT MEMBER CATEGORY

[Category 1 dan Category 2 Government Officials memiliki status hukum khusus dan, saat bertindak dalam lingkup tugas resmi mereka, tidak tunduk pada perlakuan hukum biasa. Mereka berhak atas perlindungan yang ditingkatkan (enhanced protection) dan imunitas resmi (official immunity). Setiap tindakan kekerasan, pemaksaan, penahanan, penculikan, atau penyanderaan terhadap mereka akan dianggap sebagai pelanggaran terhadap otoritas pemerintah (offense against governmental authority).]

CATEGORY 1  CONSTITUTIONAL OFFICERS

Pejabat yang jabatan, wewenang, dan eksistensinya secara eksplisit ditetapkan oleh Konstitusi Negara Bagian. Pejabat-pejabat ini menjalankan kekuasaan kedaulatan inti dari pemerintah dan beroperasi pada tingkat otoritas tertinggi di dalam cabang kekuasaan mereka masing-masing.

  • President of San Andreas
  • Vice President of San Andreas
  • Attorney General
  • Deputy Attorney General
  • Chief of Justice
  • Deputy Chief of Justice
  • Secretary of State
  • San Andreas State Legislature

CATEGORY 2  EXECUTIVE APPOINTED OFFICIALS

Pejabat yang ditunjuk oleh constitutional officers untuk menjalankan fungsi eksekutif, administratif, regulatif, atau penegakan hukum, dan bertanggung jawab secara langsung kepada otoritas eksekutif.
  • Chief of Police
  • County Sheriff
  • Police Commissioner
  • Justice Judge
  • Medical Commissioner
  • State Attorney
  • Correctional head warden

CATEGORY 3  GOVERNMENT OPERATIVE OFFICERS

Pejabat pemerintah yang menjalankan fungsi operasional sehari-hari (day to day), penegakan hukum, penuntutan, atau fungsi pendukung. Mereka bertindak di bawah pengawasan otoritas eksekutif yang lebih tinggi dan tanpa memiliki wewenang pembuatan kebijakan secara mandiri (independent policy-making power).
  • Assistant State Attorney
  • Police Officer
  • Deputy Sheriff
  • State Trooper
  • Correctional Officer
  • Medical Officer
  • Government Staff

PRINCIPLES OF CRIMINAL LIABILITY

CHAPTER 4 CULPABILITY

Section 4.1 – Definition of Culpability

  • “Culpability” – Adalah tingkatan di mana seseorang dapat dimintai pertanggungjawaban secara hukum atas tindakan atau kelalaian (omissions) mereka berdasarkan hukum yang berlaku.

Section 4.2 – Levels of Culpability

  • Intent – Keputusan sadar untuk melakukan suatu tindakan dengan tujuan mencapai hasil tertentu yang melawan hukum.
  • Knowledge – Kesadaran bahwa perilaku seseorang memiliki sifat tertentu atau adanya keadaan tertentu yang membuat tindakan tersebut menjadi melanggar hukum.
  • Recklessness – Bertindak dengan sengaja mengabaikan risiko yang besar dan tidak dapat dibenarkan, di mana tindakan tersebut dapat mengakibatkan bahaya atau konsekuensi ilegal.
  • Negligence – Kegagalan untuk berhati-hati seperti yang seharusnya dilakukan orang normal dalam situasi yang sama, yang mengakibatkan bahaya atau konsekuensi yang melanggar hukum.
Section 4.3 – Special Culpability Doctrines
  • “Strict Liability” – Tanggung jawab hukum atas suatu tindakan tanpa memandang intent, knowledge, atau negligence. Biasanya diterapkan pada pelanggaran hukum tertentu (statutory offenses).
  • “Willful Blindness” – Secara sengaja menghindari pengetahuan tentang suatu fakta atau keadaan demi melarikan diri dari tanggung jawab hukum.
  • “Complicity” – Partisipasi dalam melakukan kejahatan dengan cara membantu, menghasut, atau mendorong orang lain untuk melakukan pelanggaran tersebut.

CHAPTER 5 GENERAL PRINCIPLES ASSOCIATED TO REQUIREMENTS & EXEMPTIONS

Section 5.1 – Legal Requirements
Seluruh individu diwajibkan untuk mematuhi state dan federal laws yang mengatur perilaku, kepemilikan, dan aktivitas di dalam yurisdiksi San Andreas. Setiap tindakan atau kelalaian (omission) yang melanggar ketentuan hukum dianggap sebagai criminal offense, kecuali jika ditentukan lain atau dikecualikan oleh undang-undang.
Section 5.2 – Licensing and Authorization
Aktivitas tertentu, termasuk namun tidak terbatas pada kepemilikan firearms, pengoperasian kendaraan khusus, atau menjalankan bisnis yang teregulasi, memerlukan valid license atau otorisasi resmi dari pemerintah. Melakukan aktivitas tersebut tanpa izin yang sah dianggap sebagai sebuah offense, kecuali jika individu tersebut masuk dalam kategori legal exemption yang diakui.

Section 5.3 – Lawful Exemptions
Lawful exemption adalah suatu keadaan yang diakui oleh undang-undang atau regulasi yang melindungi seseorang dari pertanggungjawaban pidana (criminal liability) atas tindakan yang seharusnya dianggap sebagai pelanggaran. Pengecualian ini dapat mencakup tugas-tugas law enforcement, tindakan darurat (emergency actions), atau aktivitas sah lainnya yang dilakukan di bawah otoritas pemerintah.

Section 5.4 – Burden of Proof for Exemptions
Individu yang mengklaim adanya exemption (pengecualian) memikul tanggung jawab untuk membuktikan bahwa pengecualian tersebut memang berlaku, kecuali jika undang-undang secara spesifik menentukan lain. Law enforcement dan pengadilan dapat meminta bukti dokumenter atau bukti kesaksian (testimonial evidence) untuk memvalidasi klaim pengecualian tersebut.
Section 5.5 – Immunity Under Law
Individu tertentu dapat diberikan imunitas dari penuntutan (immunity from prosecution) di bawah kondisi spesifik yang diatur oleh hukum, termasuk pejabat pemerintah yang bertindak dalam lingkup tugas mereka, orang-orang yang bekerja sama di bawah immunity agreements, atau individu yang dilindungi oleh ketentuan imunitas hukum lainnya.
